name: Noripterus
sum: Lighter-built dsungaripterid from the Early Cretaceous of Xinjiang, China, living alongside Dsungaripterus.
wsnote: Maximum about 4 m if ‘Phobetor’ material from Mongolia is included.
holotype: IVPP V.4062 — Lianmuqin Formation, Junggar Basin, Xinjiang.
material: Front of skull and lower jaws, vertebrae, partial limbs and pelvis; further material including an almost complete skull (GIN 100/31, ‘Phobetor’).
biology: Toothless beak tip for probing and picking up prey, and teeth further back for cracking shells; its slenderer teeth suggest a different niche from Dsungaripterus around inland lakes.
author: Young 1973
